headline: Local Ship Captain Navigating Strait Of Hormuz Starts Carrying A 'Just In Case' Canoe On Deck
body:
Captain Ravi Subramaniam, who has spent twenty years hauling bulk shipping containers through the Strait of Hormuz, has begun bolting a bright red, six-foot plastic canoe to the bow of his three-hundred-meter cargo ship. The veteran mariner explained that since international economists have started predicting the waterway could become 'worthless' within two years due to shifting global tensions, he prefers to be prepared for the moment the route is officially declared a glorified puddle.

"I’m just being pragmatic," said Subramaniam while applying extra duct tape to the canoe’s hull. "The analysts say the geopolitical situation is volatile enough that global trade might just abandon this stretch of water entirely. If the tankers stop moving and the whole area loses its status as a critical energy corridor, I don't want to be caught on a massive vessel with nowhere to go. At least with the canoe, I can paddle my way to the nearest duty-free shop and start a new life as a professional kayak instructor."

Subramaniam’s crew reports that the ship’s daily routine has shifted significantly, with mandatory 'abandon-ship-to-canoe' drills being held every Tuesday morning. While the logistics company managing the vessel initially questioned the equipment requisition form—which categorized the canoe as 'Emergency Strategic Exit Infrastructure'—they eventually approved it after seeing the captain’s detailed PowerPoint presentation on the future of maritime insignificance.
caption: Captain Ravi is really taking the 'worthless' rumors to heart. Is it genius or just intense pessimism? 🚣‍♂️🚢 #Shipping #HormuzStrait #MaritimeLife (satire)
igHook: Would you start paddling if you heard your commute was becoming 'worthless'?
